title: streaming session keepalive bypasses metering leading to unbilled tokens
creator: Priya Anand
description: In certain long-lived streaming requests (WebSocket/HTTP2 stream + keepalive pings), periodic keepalive frames are handled by a lightweight path that does not invoke the standard metering/meter-increment middleware. This results in subsequent tokens generated by the same session being served without corresponding meter increments, causing underbilling and quota misaccounting for affected tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a streaming session with an API key tied to a per-key daily quota and low remaining balance (e.g., 50 tokens).
2) Send an initial request that consumes ~20 tokens (metered normally).
3) Keep the stream open and emit keepalive frames every 30s for several minutes.
4) Trigger a new generation request on the same session after keepalives; observe that the response consumes tokens but the meter in the billing system is not incremented for some of these requests.
5) Repeat and correlate with edge/ingress logs to confirm missing meter increments on requests that followed recent keepalives.
observed_behavior: Tokens are served and logs show model invocations and token counts, but the billing meter (per-key usage counter) does not always receive the increment. Affected requests are indistinguishable to the user but result in escaping quota enforcement and undercounting usage in billing exports.
expected_behavior: Every request that results in token generation (including requests arriving over long-lived streams after keepalive frames) must be accounted for by the meter system and should decrement or charge the appropriate quota bucket.
impact: High impact for customers using streaming APIs and keepalive patterns. Can lead to quota breaches, unexpected overuse, and revenue loss. A subset of high-throughput customers using persistent connections could underpay by a material amount over time.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01: Triage — reproduced with local harness using WS mock server. Keepalives are handled by ingress health path (fast-path) which short-circuits to connection manager.

2026-03-02: Correlation — found that requests arriving 'within X ms' after a keepalive are sometimes routed to a fast-path handler that bypasses middleware chain 'meter-increment' for performance reasons.

2026-03-03: Edge logs — ingress request_id mapping shows two request_ids for the same session: keepalive frames use control_id, generation requests use work_id; billing pipeline expects work_id but fast-path preserves only control_id in some traces.

2026-03-04: Hypothesis — a race between keepalive ACK processing and request-context hydration can cause the per-request context (which carries the meter hook) to be omitted; fallback path serves request without increment.
2026-03-05: Load test — under high concurrency, the rate of missed increments increases. Deterministic repro when keepalive < 100ms before request.
repro_logs: [ingress] session=svc-12345 conn=abcde request start ts=2026-03-01T14:12:05.190Z path=/v1/stream/gen (fast-path)
[billing] received usage update request_id=control-22222 ignored (no mapping for work-98765)
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 (WIP: add middleware instrumentation for streaming fast-path)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/401 (fix: ensure request context hydration on control->work transition)
proposed_solution: 1) Fail-fast: Instrument fast-path handlers to call the metering hook synchronously before delegating to serving runtime.
2) Robust fix: Ensure request-context hydration is transactional — create a reconciliation step that maps control_id to work_id in the billing pipeline for 5s after keepalives.
3) Add a server-side audit job to backfill missing meter increments by replaying runtime call logs into billing for the incident window.
4) Add unit/integration tests: simulate keepalive + generation interleaving, assert meter increments are emitted for every generation event.
5) Telemetry: Add a counter metric 'metering.misses.stream_keepalive' and a tracing span for context hydration to make future regressions detectable.
acceptance_criteria: All streaming generation requests increment the billing meter in integration tests that include keepalives.
Metric 'metering.misses.stream_keepalive' is instrumented and returns to 0 under synthetic regression tests.
Backfill job runs for the identified incident window and produces reconciled usage report for affected orgs.
PRs merged: runtime instrumentation + ingress hydration + billing reconciliation job; smoke-tested on staging with simulated high-frequency keepalives.
